title: Geo GPU activation timeline and mitigation notes — Q1 2027
content:
Purpose:
This is an ops-oriented activation timeline + mitigation playbook for the next tri-region GPU onboarding wave (NA / EU / APAC). Focus is on week-by-week activation windows, immediate validations, and short-circuit mitigations to prevent downstream customer impact. Document is intentionally tactical — contains runbook steps that SRE/Capacity/Platform teams will follow during activation windows.

Executive summary (one-liner):
We plan a phased activation across NA, EU, APAC from 2027-01-11 through 2027-03-05 to add ~6.8k equivalent GPU units to the fleet with a 12% warm pool and automatic throttles; primary mitigation is progressive warm-pool scaling + cross-region spillover to reserved burst capacity.

High-level capacity forecast (by region) — planned usable GPU-equivalents (unit = 1 x 40GB A100 equivalent):
- NA: target online 3,200 units total. Week 1 baseline 1,900 -> Week 8 steady 3,200.
- EU: target online 2,200 units total. Week 1 baseline 1,200 -> Week 8 steady 2,200.
- APAC: target online 1,400 units total. Week 1 baseline 700 -> Week 8 steady 1,400.
Total incremental capacity: +6,500 planned; rounded to ~6.8k with reserve and testing lanes.

Assumptions and notes:
- Units are normalized to A100-40GB perf. Mixed vendor fleet (NVIDIA, vendor-accelerated variants) will be abstracted via capacity profiles.
- Expected steady-state fleet utilization target: 55–60% average across regions at launch; safe headroom target = >= 35% free capacity to absorb bursts.
- Warm pool configuration: warm pool = 12% of region target (min 80 units in small regions).
- Default autoscaler policy: scale-up when 70% sustained CPU/GPU utilization for 10m across control plane routes; scale down after 30m of <40% utilization.
- Billing commit windows for Dedicated customers may require fixed capacity reservations; scheduling avoids those zones in weeks with active customer migrations.

Phased activation timeline (execution windows and owners):
- Prep week (2027-01-04 -> 2027-01-10): inventory, test-images, kube configs validated. Owner: Platform Eng (Thomas).
- NA wave 1 (2027-01-11 -> 2027-01-17): bring online 800 units; enable warm pool=12%; smoke test via canary ping and sample workloads. Owner: Infra Oncall (Diego).
- EU wave 1 (2027-01-18 -> 2027-01-24): bring online 600 units; validation: multi-az routing and data-plane throughput. Owner: SRE-EU (Mei).
- APAC wave 1 (2027-01-25 -> 2027-01-31): bring online 420 units; validation: regional latency sampling and KV cache priming. Owner: Infra APAC lead.
- NA wave 2 (2027-02-01 -> 2027-02-07): +800 units (reach ~1,900) with expanded warmpool.
- EU wave 2 (2027-02-08 -> 2027-02-14): +600 units.
- APAC wave 2 (2027-02-15 -> 2027-02-21): +280 units.
- Final ramp (2027-02-22 -> 2027-03-05): finish remaining units, enable cross-region routing policies and scale testing.

Weekly checklist (to be completed before mark-as-green):
1) Infra provisioning: all instances reported healthy in vendor portal + inventory matching CPI.
2) Networking: BGP/ad routes installed, new subnets advertised, internal DNS entries present.
3) KMS & secrets: workloads verified to access keys with correct IAM role.
4) Smoke tests: latency p50/p95 within expected delta (+/- 15% of baseline).
5) E2E: at least 3 customer-facing test flows (chat, embeddings, batch) validated end-to-end.
6) Telemetry sanity: token-level cost, per-route latency, model-KPIs visible in Console for new hosts.

KPIs & triggers (thresholds that trigger mitigations):
- Trigger A (Scale Stress): sustained regional GPU utilization > 82% for 12m => action: pause further activation in region, expand warm pool by +6% immediately, open capacity overflow to cross-region reserve.
- Trigger B (Latency regression): p95 token latency increase > 30% above baseline for 10m => action: roll back last activation step, route new traffic to previous stable model variants and enable two-tier fallback.
- Trigger C (Control-plane errors): > 2% 5xx rate on control-plane API for 5m => action: circuit breaker on new nodes, throttle non-critical routes, page oncall.

Mitigation playbook (ordered):
1) Fast rollback: drain new hosts, replace with warm-pool nodes or move customer routes to older pools.
2) Cross-region spillover: if warm-pool insufficient, route lower-priority/PLG traffic to alternate region (region-routing policy Delta-1).
3) Autoscaler tuning: temp reduce batch windows and increase parallel workers to reduce per-call latency.
4) Quantization/Model-fallback: switch heavy models to slightly lower perf variants (e.g., quantized v2) for a rolling 20–40% of traffic in affected routes.
5) Vendor swap (last resort): reassign workloads to alternative vendor availability zone (requires 30–90m lead time).

Observability & test harness:
- Daily dashboard snapshot to be posted in #infra-capacity with: region utilization heatmap, warm-pool fill %, deployment delta, top 5 routes by token cost.
- Synthetic workloads: run 6 load profiles for 30m each after any activation step (burst, steady, tail, long-context, embedding-heavy, short-chat).
- Canary tags: each activation attaches canary tag + git sha for tracing.

Cost & contract considerations:
- Short-term vendor burst usage estimated 2–4% of monthly bill during ramp. Finance contact: Ravi Shah.
- Reserved capacity purchases to be finalized by 2027-01-20 for NA and EU (APAC decision deferred one week).

Post-activation validation (72h window):
- Confirm 72h of stable telemetry: utilization within target band, <=0.5% error rate uplift, cost per token within forecast +/- 8%.
- Evals: run regression prompts against baseline eval set. If quality drift >1.5% on key prompts, initiate rollback.

Communication plan:
- Pre-day notice: 24h email to affected teams (GTM, CS, Sales eng) summarizing customer-impact window and mitigation controls.
- Live updates: #infra-capacity channel, hourly update cadence during activation windows.
- Post-mortem: within 72h if any trigger fired.

Open risks / questions (owner and ETA):
- Q1: APAC vendor onboarding SLA ambiguous for GPU model X (Owner: Mei Lin, ETA 2027-01-12).
- Q2: Need final sign-off on reserved capacity budget for EU (Owner: Ravi Shah, ETA 2027-01-20).
- Q3: Validation harness needs additional long-context tests for new model kernels (Owner: Research infra, ETA 2027-01-14).

Action items (immediate):
- Diego: finalize warm-pool autoscaler flags and add emergency +6% warm-pool toggle (Due 2027-01-06).
- Mei: validate APAC routing with vendor and provide failover timeline (Due 2027-01-08).
- Thomas: confirm canary image signing and update deployment playbook with rollback hooks (Due 2027-01-07).

Appendix — quick numeric runbook (compact):
- Warm pool targets: NA 380, EU 264, APAC 168 (12% of region target, floor 80).
- Test lanes reserved (per region): 8 lanes (each lane ~12 units) for soak and repro.
- Expected incremental token capacity (first 30 days): ~2.1B tokens/day across regions.

References & links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1234 (activation spec).
- Jira epic: JIRA-INFRA-789.
- Slack channel: #infra-capacity.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep early activations conservative, prefer more warm-pool than fewer surprise spins.
- If we see a persistent p95 regression, suspect kernel mismatch or KV cache priming issue before blaming hardware.
- Communicate nuance to sales (dedicated customers) — migrations may be staggered independently to avoid commitment violations.

End of doc.
